sn47.2:2.1: “Aware” (_sampajāna_), rendered in its noun form as “situational awareness”, is linguistically similar to _paññā_, “wisdom”. However it is used in context as a pragmatic understanding, not liberating insight (see also [dn9:17.9](), [mn122:9.5]()).
sn47.2:3.2: “Situational awareness” (_sampajañña_) understands the context and purpose of activities. The main examples here illustrate the activities of daily monastic life: leaving the monastery on almsround, restraint while in the town, care wearing the robes, then mindfully eating and going to the toilet.
